 News Flash
 Six Things to Know about the November 3 General Election in Loudoun
 Elections
 Posted on October 26, 2026 
 A general election will be held in Loudoun County Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election officials remind voters of six key things to know ahead of the election.
 1. Know Where to Vote 
 Voters will vote at their normal polling place on Election Day. A list of polling places in Loudoun is available at loudoun.gov/polls .  
 Anyone who is not sure about where to vote may check their voter registration card or look up their polling place and related information online at vote.elections.virginia.gov . 
 Curbside voting is available at all polling places for individuals who have mobility issues. 
 Note that the Office of Elections and Voting Registration is not a polling place on Election Day.
 2. Know When to Vote 
 Polls in Loudoun County will be open from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Tuesday, November 3.
 The last day to vote early in person is Saturday, October 31. Locations and hours for early voting are online at loudoun.gov/VoteEarly .
 Completed absentee ballots may be returned by mail (postmarked no later than November 3) or dropped off at the 24/7 drop box at the Office of Elections and Voter Registration, 750 Miller Drive SE, Suite 150, Leesburg and at early voting sites during operating hours. Ballots may also be deposited in secure drop boxes at any Loudoun County Public Library branch (except the Law Library) during business hours through October 31. 
 Voters may also drop off their ballots at any polling place up to 7:00 p.m. on November 3.
 3. Bring Identification 
 Voters will be asked to show an acceptable form of identification , such as a Virginia DMV-issued driver’s license. Voters who do not have an acceptable form of ID can sign a statement affirming their identity and they will be able to vote a regular ballot.  
 4. Know What is on the Ballot 
 Offices on the November 3 general election ballot in Loudoun will include the U.S. Senate, the 10th District Congressional District seat, and mayor and town council members in Hamilton, Hillsboro, Leesburg, Lovettsville and Purcellville. Three proposed amendments to the Virginia Constitution and three Loudoun County government bond questions will also be on the ballot. View sample ballots at loudoun.gov/SampleBallots . 
 5. Know Who Can Vote 
 All registered voters in Loudoun County are eligible to vote in the general election.
 Although the deadline to register to vote in the November 3 election or to update current voter registration information was October 23, voters may register up to and on Election Day and vote a provisional ballot. Information about same-day voter registration is available from the  Virginia Department of Elections .      
 6. Stay Informed and Know How and When to Get Election Results  
 Text LCVOTES to 888777 to receive text alerts from the Loudoun County Office of Elections and Voter Registration or sign up for the Election Update category through Alert Loudoun , the county’s email and text notification system. 
 Follow the Office of Elections and Voter Registration on social media, including Facebook , X , Bluesky and Instagram . Loudoun County Government also posts general information on Facebook , X , Bluesky and Instagram .
 Get election results: Preliminary results of voting in Loudoun County in Tuesday’s election will be available following the closing of the polls on election night at loudoun.gov/ElectionResults .
 More Information 
 More information about the November 3 general election is online at loudoun.gov/Upcoming Elections . General information about voting in Loudoun County is online at loudoun.gov/vote .
